chunks.arabic_text: بِإِسْنَادِهِ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Via his chain to Sa'd ibn Abdallah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنْ يَأْمُرَ لِي بِقَمِيصٍ أَعِدَّهُ لِكَفَنِي فَبَعَثَ بِهِ إِلَيَّ فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ؟ فَقَالَ انْزِعْ أَزْرَارَهُ

translations.en: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to order a shirt for me to prepare as my shroud, so he sent it to me. I asked: How should I prepare it? He said: Remove its buttons.

en.summary: Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' narrates that he asked Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) for a shirt to use as his shroud. When asked how to prepare it, the Imam instructed him to remove the buttons, indicating a specific legal ruling or recommended practice regarding the preparation of burial garments. This detail highlights the Shia emphasis on simplicity and the removal of extraneous adornments in the burial cloth (kafan), aligning with the prophetic tradition of returning to the earth in a state of purity and humility, free from worldly attachments.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on buttons in a Muslim's shroud according to the Imams?
